svg.text: CADENCE: superposing a structural intensity with a recurrence intensity built from full inter-arrival statistics
d = 200 · 3 multi-span GCN layers · history H = 10 (5 on GDELT) · 5.96 M parameters · one batch = one timestamp
ENTITY STATE E(t) ∈ ℝ^{N×d}, GRU-carried across t
LayerNorm, not BatchNorm: a batch is one
every entity is scored — no candidate restriction
this branch alone reaches 46.5 MRR on YAGO,
which is why the second branch is needed
Recurrence Intensity Unit — this paper's contribution, shown in full
λ_rec is a free function of thirteen inter-arrival statistics, not a decay in Δt alone
Observed occurrence history of each candidate
Thirteen statistics, read off the timelines
precomputed on a CSR index · no gradient · no entity ordering assumed
Ablation to a monotone kernel log a + p·log1p(count) − b·Δt, everything else held fixed:
Reported honestly: blanking the phase feature alone changes blocked-stratum H@1 by less than 0.6 on every dataset,
so the gain comes from the unconstrained functional form, not from any single engineered signal. Phase was removed.
superposing point processes adds intensities, so the branches are combined in log-space
There is no learned weight between the two
branches, so there is no gate that can collapse
onto one of them during training — a failure
mode reported for gated two-branch TKG models.
α = 0 on YAGO — measured, deep supervision costs 0.87 MRR there
and raises the seed std from 0.04 to 0.42; α = 0.3 elsewhere.
time-aware filtered · ties at their average position
Evaluation protocol verified against the RE-GCN reference implementation on all four datasets: zero filter disagreements over 4 000 sampled queries each.
